log.text: Light Screen up on P1's side

decisions.rationale: Altaria+Grimm lead blanks Drizzle, sets TW/screens, burns physical threats. Gengar+Ape back for Shadow Tag trap and Defiant/Ghost answers to Medi/Gyarados/steels.
decisions.notebook: Matchup build: Opp rain (Pelipper DampRock) + Arch Stamina, Intimidate Gyarados LO Adamant, Mega Medicham, Aegislash Quiet Sash, Corvi MirrorArmor. Cloud Nine Altaria blanks Drizzle + TW/Roost/WoW glue. Mega Gengar + Prankster Grimm speed control/trap. Annihilape (Ghost immunity + Defiant) answers Medi/Gyarados and hits steels. Prioritize Altaria+Grimm leads vs rain cores; Gengar+Annihilape flex. Screens Light Clay strong vs physical Medi/Gyarados. Burn Medi/Gyarados high priority. Keep Reflect vs physicals. Shadow Tag after removing Gyarados. Aegislash Blade Sash KS/SB/SS/Protect. Gyarados burned LO; Pelipper weak to Moonblast.

decisions.rationale: Down0-1; lead Medicham (Mega turn1) + Gyarados. Fake Out flinches Gengar, blocking Shadow Ball; Earthquake hits Gengar SE and spreads. Intimidate lowers physical partners. Back Archaludon (Stamina/Leftovers) and Aegislash (Focus Sash/Shadow Sneak) cover bulk and revenge. Drop Pelipper (rain suppressed by Altaria Cloud Nine) and Corviknight.
decisions.notebook: Aegislash cycle: Shield -> Shadow Ball (Blade) -> King's Shield revert; never stay Blade without revert plan. Focus Sash saves one KO hit. Gyarados burn halves physical damage; Dragon Dance cancels burn penalty for Waterfall. Cloud Nine suppresses rain, so Hurricane is70% accurate. Don't waste switches in best-of-3; switch only when ally is about to fall or for key Intimidate. Save Gyarados Intimidate for critical moments. Pelipper is fragile at low HP. Medicham Mega Evolve on entry for Pure Power and Speed132-167; Fake Out stops Gengar Shadow Ball turn1. Earthquake spread hits Gengar SE (Ground vs Poison). Shadow Tag traps both; trade Medicham for Gengar KO if needed. Archaludon Stamina + Leftovers walls special hits. Aegislash Shadow Sneak priority hits Gengar after Sash. Avoid switching except for Intimidate or faint replacement.

decisions.rationale: Reflect (Prankster +1) blunts Mega Medi Pure Power CC and LO Gyarados before their attacks. WoW Gyarados burns the Life Orb sweeper through Intimidate. Cloud Nine already blanks rain; Light Clay screens + burn is the durable answer to this physical lead.

Medicham (145 Spe) outspeeds Grimmsnarl (80-112) and should use its only first-turn Fake Out (+3 priority) to flinch the Prankster screen/setup threat while Mega Evolving into Medicham-Mega for Pure Power. Gyarados (133 Spe) outspeeds Altaria (100-132) and should Dragon Dance now to boost Atk/Spe for a sweep rather than using weak spread Waterfall/Earthquake that also hits Medicham. This stops Grimmsnarl's Reflect/Light Screen/Spirit Break and sets up both attackers safely.
decisions.notebook: Medicham Mega Evolve on entry for Pure Power and Speed132-167; Fake Out only works turn1 and stops Prankster Grimmsnarl. Gyarados Intimidate already applied; save for critical moments, Dragon Dance cancels burn penalty for Waterfall. Aegislash cycle: Shield -> Shadow Ball (Blade) -> King's Shield revert; never stay Blade without revert plan. Focus Sash saves one KO hit. Shadow Tag traps both; trade Medicham for Gengar KO if needed. Archaludon Stamina + Leftovers walls special hits. Avoid switching except for Intimidate or faint replacement.

decisions.rationale: Moonblast Medi for SE chip while Reflect goes up vs physical Medi/Gyara. Burned LO Gyara is neutered; Prankster Reflect first. Tailwind next if needed. Screens + Cloud Nine control physical rain core.

Grimmsnarl will likely Prankster Reflect first; Gyarados Dragon Dances to +2 Atk/Spe, fully negating burn damage next turn. Medicham outspeeds Altaria and should Close Combat Grimmsnarl to pressure/KO it even through Reflect, avoiding wasted setup.
decisions.notebook: Medicham Mega Pure Power doubles Atk stat; Gyarados Dragon Dance +2 cancels burn damage multiplier; Aegislash cycle KingsShield -> ShadowBall -> KingsShield revert; never stay Blade without revert plan; Focus Sash saves one KO; Shadow Tag traps both foes; Archaludon Stamina + Leftovers walls special hits; Intimidate saved for critical switch-ins; avoid switching except for Intimidate or faint replacement.

decisions.rationale: Moonblast KOs 28% Medi through -Def; Reflect+burn neuters Gyarados into Altaria. Grimm dies to any hit at 4%, so pivot to Annihilape (CC immune, answers both). Screens already up; remove Mega now.

Grimmsnarl is at4% HP and both our active outspeed it (Gyarados266, Medicham167 vs foes <=132). Medicham Close Combat is neutral vs Dark/Fairy and KO's even through Reflect (halved physical still >4%). Gyarados Waterfall also KO's Grimmsnarl; if Grimmsnarl Fake Outs one, the other still hits. Targeting Altaria is poor (Reflect + Water0.5x, Fighting0.5x). Earthquake hits ally Medicham at28% HP. Switching forfeits the KO. Both strike Grimmsnarl to guarantee removal.
decisions.notebook: Medicham-Mega Pure Power doubles Atk; Gyarados Dragon Dance +2 cancels burn damage multiplier; Aegislash cycle KingsShield -> ShadowBall -> KingsShield revert; never stay Blade without revert plan; Focus Sash saves one KO; Shadow Tag traps both foes; Archaludon Stamina + Leftovers walls special hits; Intimidate saved for critical switch-ins; avoid switching except for Intimidate or faint replacement; Reflect on opponent halves physical damage—favor special or switch to Aegislash/Archaludon; Medicham is fragile at low HP, prioritize eliminating threats before it falls; maintain Gyarados +2 pressure.

decisions.rationale: Switch Aegislash in for fainted Medicham; keep Gyarados. Aegislash is immune to Annihilape's Close Combat (Fighting vs Ghost) and takes reduced physical damage from Ice Punch/U-turn/Rage Fist thanks to Reflect and Steel/Ghost typing. Focus Sash guarantees survival against a potential KO, letting it cycle Kings Shield -> Shadow Ball -> revert. Shadow Ball is special, ignoring Reflect, and hits Annihilape super-effectively (Ghost). Gyarados remains active with +2 Atk/Spe to maintain pressure and I
decisions.notebook: Aegislash immune to Fighting (Close Combat) and benefits from Reflect on physical hits; use KingsShield -> ShadowBall -> KingsShield cycle, never stay Blade without revert plan; Focus Sash saves one KO. Shadow Ball bypasses Reflect and hits Ghost/Fighting foes super-effectively. Archaludon takes SE Fighting and has weak SpD vs Fairy special hits; prefer Aegislash as switch-in under Reflect. Gyarados Dragon Dance +2 maintains speed/attack pressure; burn halves physical damage but boosts remain; avoid Earthquake hitting ally Aegislash. Intimidate saved for critical switch-ins; avoid unnecessary switches except for faint replacement or Intimidate value. Maintain special-attacker presence when Reflect is active.

decisions.rationale: Rage Fist (BP100 post-hit) breaks Aegislash Sash through Shield forme; Tailwind enables outspeeding +2 LO Gyarados next turns. Burn+Reflect lets Ape live Waterfall; Aegislash SB/SS manageable. Chip Gyarados later.
Annihilape fainted; bring full HP Gengar (Mega/Shadow Tag option) over 4% Grimm. Aegi 1% dies to almost anything; Gyarados burned +Reflect+TW favors Gengar pressure/trap setup next. Altaria passes.

Gyarados (speed 266) outspeeds all active foes; Waterfall chips Annihilape despite burn. Aegislash then Shadow Balls (special, ignores Reflect, SE vs Fighting/Ghost) to likely KO the weakened Annihilape. Focus Sash saves Aegislash from Rage Fist. Avoid Earthquake to not hit ally. Keep pressure and deny Tailwind setup by removing threat.
decisions.notebook: Aegislash immune to Fighting; King's Shield -> Shadow Ball -> King's Shield cycle; never stay Blade without revert plan; Focus Sash saves one KO. Shadow Ball bypasses Reflect and hits Ghost/Fighting super-effectively. Gyarados DD +2 maintains speed/attack; burn halves physical damage but boosts remain; avoid Earthquake hitting ally Aegislash. Intimidate for critical switch-ins only; avoid unnecessary switches except faint replacement or Intimidate value. Maintain special attacker presence under Reflect.

decisions.rationale: Gengar outspeeds and Tbolt KOs burned 56% Gyarados even pre-mega; Mega for Shadow Tag/spa. Altaria Moonblasts 1% Aegislash first (outspeeds) for free KO unless Protect/KS. Covers double KO; if Aegi protects, Gyara still dies and Tag traps.

Aegislash is Blade-form at 1% HP with no sash; any hit KOs it, so switch to full-HP Archaludon (Ghost immune to Shadow Tag if Gengar mega evolves) to preserve presence and bring a Reflect-ignoring special attacker. Gyarados is burned and likely targeted by Gengar Thunderbolt (4x, ~77-160%); Protect (+4 priority) blocks it before it acts, saving the +2 boosts. Shadow Ball/Sneak are either too slow (priority 0, dies first) or physical and halved by Reflect; Earthquake hits ally. This maximizes sur
decisions.notebook: Aegislash re-enters in Shield form; never stay Blade without revert plan. Archaludon is special attacker that bypasses Reflect with Flash Cannon. Gyarados burn halves physical damage but stat boosts remain; avoid Earthquake when ally present. Intimidate only on switch-in. Mega Gengar Shadow Tag does not trap Ghost-types (Aegislash). Maintain special pressure under Reflect; preserve Focus Sash knowledge (already consumed).

decisions.rationale: Gengar Tbolt KO range on burned LO Gyara (4x); Alt Moonblast chips Arch (Stamina). TW remains; Reflect up. Shadow Tag locks. Prioritize removing +2 Gyara before it EQ/Waterfall.

selection: Protect [success rate reduced: Protected last turn]
decisions.rationale: Shadow Tag traps both active non-Ghosts, so Gyarados cannot switch. Gyarados is burned (physical damage halved) and at51% HP; Mega Gengar outspeeds it and Thunderbolt is4x SE, likely KO. Protect gives a50% chance to survive the hit despite consecutive-use reduction. Archaludon should bypass Reflect with special damage; Flash Cannon into Gengar-Mega is neutral and the best damage option (Dragon Claw is physical and Reflect-halved). Targeting Gengar reduces the main threat while Gyarados stalls.
decisions.notebook: Mega Gengar Shadow Tag traps non-Ghost allies; never switch into it without Ghost immunity. Archaludon is special attacker that bypasses Reflect with Flash Cannon. Gyarados burn halves physical damage but stat boosts remain; avoid Earthquake when ally present. Intimidate only on switch-in. Aegislash re-enters in Shield form; never stay Blade without revert plan. Focus Sash on Aegislash is already consumed. Maintain special pressure under Reflect; preserve Protect success-rate tracking for consecutive uses.

decisions.rationale: Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Gengar outspeeds Aeg on prio 0 so SB KOs 1% before any SB; only SS moves first and Reflect keeps it far from KO at 61%. Shadow Tag traps both. WoW Arch cuts Dragon Claw while Reflect still up; chip/spa drop less urgent than burn.

Shadow Tag after removing Gyarados. Aegislash Blade Sash KS/SB/SS/Protect. Gyarados burned LO; Pelipper weak to Moonblast. Arch Careful Leftovers Stamina DC/FC/Protect/SR.

decisions.rationale: Archaludon is Shadow-Tag trapped and slower than both foes (105 vs 200-400), so without priority it dies to Shadow Ball/Moonblast before acting; Protect (+4) lets it block and survive. Aegislash is 1% HP and also slower, but Shadow Sneak (+1) strikes before foes act, letting it chip super-effective damage into 60% Gengar-Mega before falling. This maximizes damage output while keeping Archaludon alive for follow-up Flash Cannon once Tailwind expires.
decisions.notebook: Shadow Tag traps non-Ghost allies; Archaludon is trapped and cannot switch. Protect/King's Shield fail only if user moves last overall, but priority +4/+1 lets slow Pokemon act before priority-0 foes despite Tailwind. Aegislash re-enters in Shield form; using an attack shifts to Blade form. Focus Sash is already consumed. Tailwind ends after this turn, removing foe speed doubles. Maintain special pressure under Reflect; Archaludon should prioritize Protect when outsped, then Flash Cannon/Dragon Claw on safe turns.

decisions.rationale: Burn Arch to cut physical damage and Stamina value; Shadow Ball chips through +2 Def while Reflect holds. Gengar outspeeds; no second foe. Avoid NVE Tbolt/immune Sludge. Roost/TW unnecessary now.
Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Gengar-Mega (21% HP) is guaranteed KO'd by Flash Cannon (special, Reflect-ignored; damage range22.8-75.6% >21%). Gengar outspeeds but Shadow Ball into Archaludon (91% HP, Stamina, Leftovers) is survivable (31.5-104.2%). Altaria's Moonblast is neutral and moderate. Dragon Claw is physical and halved by Reflect. Protect has reduced success and delays the KO. Eliminating Gengar now creates a winnable1v1 vs Altaria after Tailwind expires.
decisions.notebook: Shadow Tag traps Archaludon; Aegislash is dead. Reflect halves physical damage for2 more turns—prioritize special moves. Tailwind ends this turn, removing foe speed doubles. Archaludon has Stamina and Leftovers for durability. Flash Cannon is optimal under Reflect. Plan: KO Gengar-Mega, then pressure Altaria with Dragon Claw/Flash Cannon once Reflect falls; avoid consecutive Protect.

decisions.rationale: Grimm 4% dies to any FC; Fake Out flinches Arch (first turn in) so he lives. Moonblast chips burned Arch (special, ignores +3 Def). Screen/Reflect won't save 4% from FC; Spirit Break too slow and physical into +3 Def. WoW redundant.

Flash Cannon is special, so it ignores both burn (halves physical Attack) and Reflect (halves physical damage). Grimmsnarl is at4% HP and takes2x from Steel, so Flash Cannon guarantees the KO (min ~43% max HP). Removing Grimmsnarl leaves only Altaria. Dragon Claw is physical and would be severely weakened (~0.25x effective). Protect wastes the KO opportunity. Aegislash is fainted, so pass.
decisions.notebook: Archaludon: Stamina + Leftovers; burn damage cancels Leftovers heal. Reflect ends after this turn; Tailwind also ends now. Flash Cannon is best move while burned and under Reflect; Dragon Claw is physical and crippled by burn. Grimmsnarl is low HP and Steel-weak. Altaria is Dragon/Flying, weak to Dragon/Ice. Shadow Tag traps Archaludon; Aegislash, Gyarados, Medicham-Mega are dead. Avoid consecutive Protect. Plan: KO Grimmsnarl now, then pressure Altaria with special attacks; consider clearing burn if possible.

selection: Light Screen (your side, including ally Altaria)
decisions.rationale: 2v1; KO Arch wins. +5 Def guts physical SB (~5-8%); MB is only real chip on 32% Arch. Prankster LS up before Arch; softens FC if it snipes 4% Grimm or hits Altaria. Burn already nerfs DC so Reflect is worse. Tailwind/Roost waste; WoW redundant.

Archaludon is burned, crippling physical Dragon Claw; Flash Cannon is special and unaffected. Grimmsnarl is at4% HP and2x weak to Steel, so Flash Cannon guarantees KO (min42.6% damage). Altaria is full HP and Dragon Claw is halved by burn, so it’s the wrong target. Aegislash is fainted, so pass. This removes the low-HP threat and lets Archaludon pressure Altaria next.
decisions.notebook: Archaludon: Stamina + Leftovers; burn cancels Leftovers heal. Reflect ends after this turn; Tailwind also ends now. Flash Cannon is best move while burned and under Reflect; Dragon Claw is physical and crippled by burn. Grimmsnarl is low HP and Steel-weak. Altaria is Dragon/Flying, weak to Dragon/Ice. Shadow Tag traps Archaludon; Aegislash, Gyarados, Medicham-Mega are dead. Avoid consecutive Protect. Plan: KO Grimmsnarl now, then pressure Altaria with special attacks; consider clearing burn if possible.

decisions.rationale: Moonblast Arch to finish 19% brn before Leftovers; only damaging option. Screens up, no need TW/Roost/WoW. Pass on fainted Grimm.

Dragon Claw is physical, so it ignores opponent Light Screen and Archaludon’s SpA -1, and is super-effective (2×) on Altaria’s Dragon typing. Burn halves physical damage, but Flash Cannon is special and doubly weakened by Light Screen and the -1 SpA stage, making it far weaker. With only Archaludon alive vs Altaria, we must chip now; Protect stalls without damage and can’t secure a KO alone. Target Altaria (slot a) since slot b is fainted.
decisions.notebook: Durable: Archaludon has Stamina + Leftovers; burn cancels Leftovers healing. Opponent Light Screen active (7 turns); Reflect and Tailwind expired. Only Altaria remains alive (Sitrus Berry, Cloud Nine). Archaludon is burned, Def +6, SpA -1, HP20%. Dragon Claw is best damage option vs Dragon/Flying despite burn; Flash Cannon is crippled by Light Screen and SpA drop. Avoid unnecessary Protect when damage is needed. Future: use physical Dragon moves against Dragon foes; watch Altaria Roost/Sitrus; try to clear burn if an opportunity arises; remember Stamina boosts Def on hits but not SpD.

decisions.rationale: Moonblast KO's 5% Arch from full legal range (special ignores +6 Def; burn/Leftovers irrelevant). Finish last foe to win game 2 and tie series.

Only Altaria remains (76% HP, Sitrus, Cloud Nine, Light Screen up). Dragon Claw is super-effective Dragon physical; despite burn it outdamages Flash Cannon, which is neutral and crippled by Light Screen + SpA -1. Protect/Stealth Rock don’t advance the win. Aegislash is fainted, so pass. Speed order is uncertain, but damage is needed now.
decisions.notebook: Durable: Archaludon Stamina + Leftovers; burn cancels Leftovers healing. Opponent Light Screen active; Reflect/Tailwind expired. Only Altaria alive (Sitrus Berry, Cloud Nine). Dragon Claw best damage vs Dragon/Flying despite burn; Flash Cannon hurt by screen and SpA drop. Avoid unnecessary Protect when damage needed. Future: prioritize physical Dragon moves vs Dragon foes; watch Altaria Roost/Sitrus; seek burn clear if possible; Stamina boosts Def on hits but not SpD.

reflections.summary: Won via Altaria Cloud Nine glue + WoW burns + Moonblast chip wearing down Stamina Archaludon behind Light Screen after Gengar/Grimm trades removed the rest.
reflections.adjustment: Preview plan (Mega Gengar + Grimm + Ape + Altaria) suited the non-rain bring well; next game still lead Altaria+Grimm but respect Arch Stamina by prioritizing early burn/chip over late 1v1.

Cloud Nine Altaria blanks Drizzle + TW/Roost/WoW glue. Mega Gengar + Prankster Grimm speed control/trap. Annihilape (Ghost immunity + Defiant) answers Medi/Gyarados and hits steels. Prioritize Altaria+Grimm leads vs rain cores; Gengar+Annihilape flex. Screens Light Clay strong vs physical Medi/Gyarados. Burn Medi/Gyarados high priority. Keep Reflect vs physicals. Shadow Tag after removing Gyarados. Aegislash Blade Sash KS/SB/SS/Protect. Gyarados burned LO; Pelipper weak to Moonblast. Arch Careful Leftovers Stamina DC/FC/Protect/SR. G2 bring: Arch/Gyarados/Aegi/MegaMedi (Pelipper+Corvi home). Arch Stamina stacks freely on resisted hits; Aegi Quiet Sash confirmed. Altaria Moonblast pressure + burn reliable vs Arch late.

reflections.summary: Lost after all allies fainted, leaving burned Archaludon to be chipped out by Altaria's Moonblast through Light Screen. The preview was wrong: Medicham-Mega was a poor mega choice—Grimmsnarl's Prankster Fake Out and dual screens neutralized it, and the team had no screen breaker, burn clear, or second late threat, so a single Stamina tank faced a Roost/Sitrus pivot alone.
reflections.adjustment: For game 3 change the four brought—drop Medicham-Mega (do not mega evolve a Fake Out-vulnerable physical sweeper) and bring a Taunt/screen-breaker or burn-immune attacker; lead with immediate Grimmsnarl pressure before screens go up, and keep a backup win condition so Archaludon isn't solo against Altaria.
reflections.notebook: Opponent core revealed: Grimmsnarl (Prankster, Light Clay, Fake Out, Reflect, Light Screen, Spirit Break) sets dual screens quickly; Altaria (Cloud Nine, Sitrus Berry, Bold, Tailwind, Roost, Will-O-Wisp, Moonblast) is a defensive burn/recovery pivot that nullifies weather and chips special attackers; Gengar-Mega (Timid, Shadow Ball/Sludge Bomb/Thunderbolt/Protect); Annihilape (Jolly, Expert Belt, Defiant, Rage Fist/Close Combat/Ice Punch/U-turn). Not brought: Primarina, Gliscor. Durable tendencies: screens up fast; Altaria burns then roosts; opponent wins via chip and recovery. Future plan: bring Taunt or Magic Bounce; KO Grimmsnarl first; avoid burn-vulnerable physical attackers; don't rely solely on Stamina/Leftovers vs sustained Moonblast; pick a Mega only if it can operate through Prankster disruption and hit through screens.
